newsitem.title: USA: Texan mother did not deny killing sons-investigator.
newsitem.headline: Texan mother did not deny killing sons-investigator.

text.p: A mother accused of killing her two sons never denied murdering them during an interrogation on the day of her arrest, an investigator testified in court on Thursday.

Private investigator Bill Parker, who questioned Darlie Routier for the Rowlett, Texas police department after she was arrested on June 18, said her responses were vague when he asked her several times if she had murdered her sons Devon, 6, and Damon, 5.
"She always had the same verbal response: 'If I did it, I don't remember'," he said. Once, he said, "she did not respond, she just shrugged her shoulders."

Prosecutors charge that Routier, 27, stabbed the boys to death while they slept in their Rowlett home near Dallas on June 6. They said she did it in fit of rage and depression about her weight problems and the family's financial difficulties.
Routier Wednesday testified that she loved the boys and did not kill them. She said an intruder who also attacked her had murdered them, then fled from the house.
Routier said the attack happened while she was asleep and she could not remember many details of that night.
A defence witness Thursday, psychiatrist Richard Coons, testified that traumatic events often cloud the memory.
Closing arguments in the three-week-long trial were set for Friday. The case was moved to Kerrville, 60 miles (95 km) northwest of San Antonio, Texas because of heavy pre-trial publicity.
If convicted, Routier could face the death penalty.
